D1.result:
8 findings (1 🔴 Important, 2 🟣 Pre-existing, 5 🟡 Nit):

1. 🔴 Important `src-tauri/src/autostart_win.rs:260`: Tandem can refuse to register start-at-login for its own copy when the profile path is spelled two different ways. `command_for_this_launch` refuses if either the canonical pair or the raw pair reads as "another profile". The raw pair compares `current_exe()`, which can keep an 8.3 short name such as `C:\Users\JANEDO~1\...` when the process was started by a short path, against `home_dir()`, which is the long `C:\Users\Jane Doe`. Fix: decide on the canonical pair alone, and use the raw pair only when canonicalising fails on both sides. Do not OR the two results.

   Failure scenario: A user named 'Jane Doe' starts Tandem through a short-name path. The canonical check says the exe is in her own profile, but the raw check sees `JANEDO~1` under `C:\Users`, not under `C:\Users\Jane Doe`, so `enable()` fails. The toggle shows `io` and the refresh at launch logs 'registration may be stale' every time.

2. 🟣 Pre-existing `src-tauri/src/autostart_win.rs:186`: Turning start-at-login on fails on a Windows profile that has no `HKCU\...\CurrentVersion\Run` key. `enable()` only opens the key with `RegOpenKeyExW` and returns `NotFound` when it is missing, instead of creating it with `RegCreateKeyExW`. `auto-launch` 0.5 behaved the same way, but this is now Tandem's own code and a test locks the behaviour in. Fix: create the Run key if it is missing (HKCU only).

   Failure scenario: On a fresh or cleaned profile without the Run key, the user turns the toggle on, gets `io`, and the toggle stays off.

3. 🟣 Pre-existing `src-tauri/src/autostart.rs:455`: Tandem can show start-at-login as on when Windows has disabled the entry. `win_startup_approved_allows` treats an entry as enabled whenever the last 8 bytes are zero, so a disabled marker (`03`) with a zero timestamp reads as enabled. A test asserts this on purpose, copying `auto-launch` 0.5. Windows decides by the first byte: an even byte is enabled and an odd byte is disabled. Fix: decide on the first byte (`bytes[0] & 1 == 0`). Check this against what Windows actually writes before changing it.

   Failure scenario: A tool writes StartupApproved `03 00 .. 00` for Tandem. Windows does not start Tandem at login, but the toggle shows on, and `refresh_registration` keeps rewriting the entry as if it were active.

4. 🟡 Nit `src-tauri/src/autostart_win.rs:215`: Turning the toggle on can report a failure when the start-at-login entry was in fact written. `enable()` writes the Run value first and then returns `Err` if writing the StartupApproved value fails. A failure to open the StartupApproved key, on the other hand, is ignored. Fix: handle a failed StartupApproved write the same way (log it and go on), or undo the Run write, so the result is consistent.

   Failure scenario: The StartupApproved key exists but the value write is denied, for example by a policy or AV hook. The Run value is written, but `autostart_set_enabled` returns the `io` error, and `refresh_registration` logs 'refresh failed (registration may be stale)' on every launch even though the Run value was refreshed.

5. 🟡 Nit `src-tauri/src/autostart.rs:477`: The check meant to stop an admin's Run entry pointing at a file a less trusted user can replace covers only user-profile folders. `exe_in_another_users_profile` refuses `C:\Users\<other>` and `C:\Users\Public`, but not other locations that every user can write, such as a folder created at the drive root or `C:\ProgramData`. The doc comment and CHANGELOG describe the protection more broadly than the code provides. Fix: narrow the stated claim, or also refuse paths outside the profile and Program Files trees that standard users can write.

   Failure scenario: An admin runs a portable copy from `C:\Tools\Tandem\tandem.exe` (Authenticated Users can modify it) and turns start-at-login on. The admin's HKCU Run entry now points at a file any local user can replace, and it runs at the admin's logon.

6. 🟡 Nit `.github/dependabot.yml:119`: Dependabot can now move macOS and Linux to `tauri-plugin-autostart` 2.7 (`auto-launch` 0.6) with no review step. The `>=2.7.0` ignore was removed and Cargo.toml now asks only for `"2"`. The new Cargo.toml comment says to re-check `uninstall_scrub.rs` `autostart_entry_path` when bumping, but the weekly grouped PR will do the bump with nothing enforcing that check. Fix: keep a dependabot ignore (or a test) for the 2.7 bump until the macOS/Linux file paths and modes under 0.6 have been checked.

   Failure scenario: A group PR bumps the lock to 2.7. If 0.6 names or places the LaunchAgent plist or the `.desktop` file differently, the uninstall scrub leaves an orphaned login item pointing at a deleted app, and nothing catches it before merge.

7. 🟡 Nit `src-tauri/src/autostart_win.rs:135`: Reading the start-at-login state can fail if the value changes between two reads. `query_value` reads the size first and then the data. If another writer makes the value longer in between, the second call returns `ERROR_MORE_DATA`, which becomes an error. Fix: retry on `ERROR_MORE_DATA` with the new length, or give the buffer some extra room.

   Failure scenario: Task Manager or another Tandem instance rewrites the value between the two calls. `autostart_get_status` reports the `io` error and shows the toggle as off for that open of Settings.

8. 🟡 Nit `src-tauri/src/autostart.rs:208`: A doc comment in `autostart_refresh_allowed` is now wrong. Its Debug bullet still says "The autostart plugin is registered with no `cfg` gate". After this PR the plugin is registered only off Windows, and the Windows registration (the HKCU `Run\Tandem` case the bullet describes) is `autostart_win.rs`. Fix: reword the bullet to refer to the backend (the plugin on macOS/Linux, `autostart_win.rs` on Windows).

   Failure scenario: Someone reading the guard's reasoning concludes the plugin is still live on Windows and misreads which code writes the Run value.

Claude rewriting a sentence that starts with a linked or bold word now turns the whole rewritten sentence into that link, or bold. Fix: confirm this is wanted for multi-word agent rewrites. Findings from the review of the staged diff in `.review-input/pr.diff`. All four angles ran. The worst one: the new docs say no request to the local server goes through an environment proxy, but `tandem license` still uses the global `fetch` and sends the buyer's licence key that way. No CLAUDE.md rule was clearly broken. I could not inspect the MCP SDK or undici code because `node_modules` is not in the checkout, so the claims about how undici and the SDK behave come from memory of those libraries.

6 findings (1 🔴 Important, 5 🟡 Nit):

1. 🔴 Important `src/cli/license.ts:446`: The new docs say every request to the local server skips the environment proxy, but `tandem license activate/deactivate` still sends its loopback POST through the global `fetch`. `postToLoopbackTandem` uses `fetchImpl = fetch`, aims it at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/license/activate`, and nothing in this PR moves it to `loopbackFetch`. Fix: default `fetchImpl` to `loopbackFetch`, or narrow the claims in docs/security.md and docs/decisions.md to the token-carrying programs.

   Failure scenario: A user has NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 and HTTP_PROXY set and runs `tandem license activate <key>` while Tandem is running. Node tunnels the POST to 127.0.0.1 through the proxy as plain-HTTP CONNECT, so the proxy can read the body (the signed licence blob and the buyer's email). The security docs this PR adds say this cannot happen ('Requests to the local server never use an environment proxy').

2. 🟡 Nit `tests/shared/loopback-fetch-seam.test.ts:1006`: The seam test that is supposed to catch a regression back to the global `fetch` only matches a direct `fetch(` call. Its regex `(^|[^\w.$])fetch\s*\(` misses `globalThis.fetch(`, `fetch` passed by reference (`fetchImpl = fetch` in src/cli/license.ts, `{ fetch }`), and `.fetch(`. The 'Reopen if' clause in docs/security.md relies on this test. Fix: also flag any bare `fetch` identifier used as a value and `globalThis.fetch` outside loopback-fetch.ts, and allow-list the known non-loopback uses explicitly.

   Failure scenario: A later change writes `const f = opts.fetchImpl ?? fetch; await f(`${url}/api/...`, { headers: { Authorization } })` in src/channel. The seam test stays green, the in-process passthrough mock hides the problem in every other suite, and the token goes through the proxy again.

3. 🟡 Nit `src/shared/loopback-fetch.ts:389`: `loopbackFetch` is typed as `typeof fetch` and `isLoopbackTarget` explicitly accepts a `Request`, but passing a global `Request` (or a global `FormData` body) to a loopback host should throw. npm undici's `fetch` only recognises its own `Request` class, so Node's built-in `Request` is turned into the string "[object Request]" and URL parsing fails. Fix: when input is a `Request`, pass `input.url` with the request's method, headers, body and signal merged into init, or convert it to undici's own `Request`. Add a test that actually fetches with a `Request`.

   Failure scenario: A caller (or a future SDK version) calls `loopbackFetch(new Request('http://127.0.0.1:3479/mcp', {...}))`. `isLoopbackTarget` returns true, `undiciFetch` throws `TypeError: Failed to parse URL from [object Request]`, and the bridge or shim request fails even though the same call works with the global `fetch`.

4. 🟡 Nit `src/shared/loopback-fetch.ts:389`: Redirects are followed inside undici on the proxy-free Agent, so a redirect from 127.0.0.1 to another host also bypasses the user's proxy. That breaks the module's claim that every other host uses the global `fetch` as before. It affects `authFetch` and the preflight, which use the default `redirect: 'follow'`. Fix: send loopback requests with `redirect: 'manual'` and re-issue a cross-host `Location` through `loopbackFetch`, or document that the whole redirect chain goes direct.

   Failure scenario: Under a non-loopback setup, or when something squatting on 127.0.0.1:3479 answers with a 302 to `http://lan-host/`, the follow-up request goes straight out instead of through the required HTTP_PROXY. Custom headers such as X-Claude-Session-Id go with it, and on a proxy-only network the request fails.

5. 🟡 Nit `src/server/launcher/run-files.ts:136`: Dropping `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY: ""` from the run MCP config removes a guard that turned Node's proxy off for the whole bridge process. Now only request paths explicitly routed through `loopbackFetch` are protected. Any SDK request that uses its own `fetch` instead of the `fetch` option, or any `node:http` request (Node 22.21+ also proxies `http.request` under this variable), now goes through the proxy where it did not before. Fix: keep the blank as defence in depth, or confirm that every request the bridge makes goes through `loopbackFetch`.

   Failure scenario: The launcher spawns Claude with NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 and HTTP_PROXY inherited, and the entry's env wins the merge. Before this PR the bridge ran with the proxy off. Now a code path the SDK does not route through `opts.fetch` (auth discovery, a future SDK change) sends headers to the proxy, and nothing tests for it.

6. 🟡 Nit `tests/cli/loopback-no-proxy.test.ts:517`: `nodeHonoursEnvProxy()` returns true for any Node major above 22, which includes 23.x. As far as I know, Node 23 does not support NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY (it came in 24.0 and was backported to 22.21), so check that before changing it. package.json `engines` (`>=22.12.0`) allows 23.x. Fix: require `maj >= 24 || (maj === 22 && min >= 21)`.

   Failure scenario: On Node 23.x the control child's global `fetch` connects directly, `tunnel.connects` stays empty, and `beforeAll`'s assertion 'the harness must be able to show a proxied request' fails the whole suite instead of skipping it.

7 findings (2 🔴 Important, 5 🟡 Nit):

1. 🔴 Important `src/client/panels/AnnotationCardActions.svelte:74`: A double-click on Remove deletes the whole thread, so the new confirmation never gets a chance to stop it. In `handleRemoveClick`, the first click arms the button and a second click a few milliseconds later passes the `removeArmed` check and calls `onRemove`, with nothing requiring the clicks to be separate. Fix: record when the button was armed and ignore a confirming click that comes within ~400ms of it (or whose `e.detail > 1`), so only a separate, deliberate second click deletes.

   Failure scenario: A resolved user comment has Claude replies, so `confirmRemove` is true. The user double-clicks Remove by habit. Click 1 sets removeArmed=true and click 2 runs onRemove(id), so the comment and every reply are deleted with no undo and the 'Delete thread?' label never shows in time to be read.

Fix: make `removeAnnotation` return success, then call `forgetResolved` only after the server confirms the delete (or after the record leaves the map).

   Failure scenario: The user resolves a comment, and Undo shows. They click Remove, the server answers 404 'No document open' (a tab swap race), and a 'Remove failed' toast appears. The two important ones:
- **Dismiss/Undo can lose a comment's own suggestion.** The Dismiss path still copies old reply-accept fields onto the record, and Undo then acts on them.
- **A bad value in one of the two new fields drops the whole annotation from disk on reload.** The on-disk format now checks their types, but the fast save path writes them unchecked.

6 findings (2 🔴 Important, 1 🟣 Pre-existing, 3 🟡 Nit):

1. 🔴 Important `src/client/panels/useAnnotationReview.svelte.ts:781`: Undoing a Dismiss (or the Accept of a plain comment) can delete or replace the comment's own suggestedText. resolveAnnotation's non-apply write `map.set(id, { ...ann, status })` keeps any stale acceptedReplyId/priorSuggestedText from the sanitized record, and undoResolveAnnotation (line 972) always runs restoredFromReplyAccept whenever acceptedReplyId is present, whatever the status. This contradicts the new doc on withoutReplyAccept ('Every revert and every accept write goes through it'). Fix: write `{ ...withoutReplyAccept(ann), status }` here, and/or only apply restoredFromReplyAccept when `ann.status === "accepted"`.

The PR's own test 'drops stale reply-accept fields' admits such leftovers exist. The user clicks Dismiss, and the record is stored as dismissed with the provenance still on it. The user clicks Undo: restoredFromReplyAccept strips suggestedText because priorSuggestedText is null. The comment comes back pending with its proposal gone. If priorSuggestedText is a stale string instead, the comment gets an unrelated proposal.

2. 🔴 Important `src/server/annotations/schema.ts:503`: One malformed acceptedReplyId or priorSuggestedText value now makes the whole annotation disappear on the next reload. Before, `.passthrough()` kept unknown fields. Now they are typed (z.string / z.string().nullable()), but sync.ts normalizeAnnotation's fast path (canonical type plus numeric rev) writes the raw Y.Map object to the envelope without validating it, and parseAnnotationDoc's filterUnreadableRows drops any row that fails the schema. Fix: strip or coerce the two fields in normalizeAnnotation before persisting, or declare them leniently (e.g. `.catch(undefined)`) so a bad value loses only the field, not the record.

   Failure scenario: Any connected client (an older or buggy build, or a hand-written Y.Map update) stores `acceptedReplyId: 7` on a comment that has rev:1. snapshot() persists it as-is. On the next server start, parseAnnotationDoc logs 'dropping unreadable annotation' and the user's comment and its thread anchor are gone for good. If it was the only annotation, the whole envelope is quarantined as corrupt.

With this PR the revert also puts priorSuggestedText back, so after a reply-accept Undo the parent is pending with its OWN proposal while the document still holds the reply's rewrite. The record goes back to pending with the original suggestedText, the document keeps the reply's text, and Undo returns true. The next Accept applies the parent's proposal on top of text it was never written against, unchecked because the record has no snapshot.

The clamp returns it unchanged. `text.slice(0, -6)` wraps to "Hello" and matches the snapshot, so the lazy arm mints an anchor at offset -6, an offset the snapshot never described, and persists it. This is the same negative-wrap bug the new `from` case fixes, now on the `to` side.

The restart's read gets a truncated or empty string, so JSON.parse throws and the file is copied to .broken-backups. The empty config means no integration is found, so the plan is null. The timer fires and `startInternal(currentEpoch)` passes every check, then spawns before or after `respawn`'s `spawnOnce`.
